title: Lorenz at the Hunting Ground
sceneText:
You did not expect to meet Lorenz at the hunting ground.

He is not hunting and he is not on a horse. He came on foot, out to the edge of the woods, and stopped beside a big oak with his hand on the bark.

There is something very quiet about him seen from behind.

He hears you come up and does not turn round.

{@lorenz}“You came.”

“I thought you did not attend the season.”

{@lorenz}“I do not,” he says. “I came for this tree.”

You ask what is particular about the tree.

{@lorenz}“The kindling for the Observance is taken from here,” he says. “All three estates take theirs from here. Maplegate, Thornwall, Millridge.”

He takes his hand off the bark.

{@lorenz}“It is not cut. We take what it drops of itself. However much comes down in a given autumn is what is taken, and in a year when little comes down the three houses divide it.”

“Why this one?”

{@lorenz}“Because the generation before us took it from here,” he says. “That is the only reason there is.”

He looks up at the crown.

{@lorenz}“A good deal has come down this year. It is a good year.”

He walks half a circle round the tree, picks up a fallen branch, looks at it, and puts it down again.

{@lorenz}“I come and look at it once every autumn. Not as a rite. Only to see that it is well.”

variants.lorenz_question:
He picks up a second fallen branch, and this time he does not put it down.

{@lorenz}“Hartmann came to me,” he says. “Here. Last autumn, also at the taking of the wood.”

You wait.

{@lorenz}“He asked me a question.” Lorenz flicks a little soil off the branch with a finger. “He asked whether, if the work a man does is itself wrong, doing that work better means being further in the wrong.”

He puts the branch into the cloth bag at his side.

{@lorenz}“He asked it very politely, as though it were something with nothing to do with him. A technical question.”

He looks up at you.

{@lorenz}“But a technical question asked that far is not a technical question any more.”

“What did you tell him?”

{@lorenz}“I said I did not know,” he says. “I still do not know.”

He draws the mouth of the bag closed.

{@lorenz}“I should have asked him then why he was asking. I did not ask.”
variants.lorenz_question_again:
He picks up a second fallen branch, looks at it, and does not put it down.

{@lorenz}“I have told you about the thing he came and asked me,” he says.

You say you remember.

{@lorenz}“It was here.” With the hand holding the branch he points at the ground. “This spot. Where he stood that day was a little to the left of where you are standing now.”

He puts the branch into the bag.

{@lorenz}“I have thought about it many times this year,” he says. “Not about what he asked.”

{@lorenz}“About why I did not ask him.”
variants.marguerite:
On the way back to camp, Marguerite’s carriage is standing at the side of the forest road. She is sitting inside with the door open.

{@marguerite}“Come up and sit a while,” she says. “I have travelled this road forty years. I do not need to look at it.”

It is warmer inside than out. She moves the rug on her knees aside.

The carriage starts.

{@marguerite}“Last night,” she says. “You need not feel you owe me anything. Henk has to do that once a year, and somebody always has to head him off.”

She looks out of the window.

{@marguerite}“Hartmann came to me as well.”

She says it in exactly the tone she used a moment ago, as though speaking about the trees along the road.

{@marguerite}“End of the summer. Late August. He came without sending word first, which was unlike him. I had tea brought, and he sat over an hour.”

“What did he say?”

{@marguerite}“He did not say,” she says. “He went round it a long while, asking about matters of estate management, very politely and very unnecessarily. He knew those things better than I do.”

{@marguerite}“I waited for him to bring out the real thing. He did not.”

The wheels go over a stretch of loose stone. She puts a hand to the window frame.

{@marguerite}“At the end he stood up and thanked me and said he had disturbed me.”

She turns her head to look at you.

{@marguerite}“I am still thinking about that day,” she says. “My judgment is that what that young man wanted to ask was not a question I could answer.”

“What question?”

{@marguerite}“I do not know,” she says. “But that he came to me means he had already asked others, and that they had not given him an answer either.”

The carriage reaches the camp turning. She raps twice on the panel and it stops.

{@marguerite}“He was a good steward,” she says. “Nobody in this part of the country ever doubted that.”

“Including him?”

She looks at you a while.

{@marguerite}“That is the question.”
